transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, hi… I came in because I just, I don’t know, I feel like there’s a motor running inside me all day. Like I can’t shut it off. If I have to sit still somewhere — like at church, or here in the clinic waiting, or even just sitting at home — I start feeling trapped, like my body is telling me I need to get up right now or do something.

It’s not just being bored, it’s more like I’m uncomfortable in my own skin when I’m supposed to stay put. I’ll try to sit there, but it builds up and builds up, and I feel like I have to move. That’s really why I’m here, because it’s getting hard to deal with.
Did this feeling start after you began taking a medication or changed the dose of one?

Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I’m not really sure how to answer that exactly, because I don’t have a clear thing in my head like, “Oh, I started this pill and then suddenly I felt like this.” It doesn’t feel that straightforward to me.

I haven’t noticed it being tied to a dose change or anything like that. Like, nobody changed something and then the next week I was bouncing off the walls or feeling worse. At least not that I can remember. It’s more just… this is kind of how I’ve been, and it gets really hard in certain situations. But if you mean like medicine causing it, I don’t have anything specific like that to point to.
Is this urge to move usually strongest in the evening or at night when you’re sitting still or lying down?

Not really like only evening or night, no. I mean, it can happen then if I’m sitting around or lying there, sure, but it’s not like it waits until nighttime. It’s more like I’ve got this motor running inside me all day.

Like I was saying, if I have to sit still at church, or sitting here in the clinic, or even at home when I’m supposed to just be relaxing, I start feeling trapped in my own body. It builds up and I feel like I have to get up, move around, do something. So it’s more about having to sit still than a certain time of day.
Have you felt this unable-to-sit-still way since you were a child?

Yeah… yeah, since I was a kid, honestly. I mean, I didn’t have words for it back then, but looking back it was the same kind of thing. In school, I was always the boy who couldn’t stay in his seat. Teachers would move me around the classroom, like putting me closer to them or away from other kids, because I’d be up before I was supposed to be, or turning around, or talking when I wasn’t supposed to.

I remember getting in trouble a lot for blurting things out or jumping up before class was done, like I just couldn’t wait until the right time. It wasn’t like I was trying to be bad exactly. I just felt like I had to move or say something right then. So yeah, this isn’t something that just started as an adult. It goes way back to when I was a boy in school.
Have you ever had a period when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’ve had nights where I don’t sleep well, like anybody does, but I wouldn’t say there’s been some stretch where I only needed a few hours and then felt great or unusually full of energy.

If I don’t sleep enough, I usually feel it. I don’t remember a time where it was like, “Wow, I barely slept and I’m totally fine, I can just keep going.” So… no, not that I’ve noticed.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about different things?

I’m not really sure how to answer that one. I mean, I worry about things sometimes, like anybody does, but I don’t know if I’d say I spend a lot of time worrying about different things.

It’s not like I’m sitting there all day going from one fear to another, at least not that I’ve really noticed. Sometimes if something is right in front of me, yeah, I’ll think about it, but I don’t know… I wouldn’t want to say yes if you mean constant worrying about everything. I’m not sure that’s really me.
